name: Looney Tunables - glibc ld.so GLIBC_TUNABLES LPE (CVE-2023-4911)
description: CVE-2023-4911 (Looney Tunables) is a buffer overflow in glibc's dynamic loader ld.so when it processes the GLIBC_TUNABLES environment variable. Because ld.so runs with elevated privileges for SUID binaries, a crafted GLIBC_TUNABLES value corrupts memory during startup of any SUID-root program and yields a local root shell. Affects glibc 2.34 through 2.38 as shipped on Fedora 37/38, Ubuntu 22.04/23.04, Debian 12/13 and others.
notes:
=== WHAT IT IS ===
  A buffer overflow in __tunables_init() when ld.so parses GLIBC_TUNABLES. SUID binaries
  still honor a sanitized tunables string, and the overflow happens before privileges drop,
  so a crafted value overwrites the saved stack/state and hijacks execution as root.

=== CHECK GLIBC VERSION ===
  ldd --version                 # 'ldd (GNU libc) 2.35' etc
  getconf GNU_LIBC_VERSION
  # Vulnerable: 2.34 - 2.38 (released 2021-08 .. 2023-07) before the 2023-10 fix.

=== TRIGGER (manual probe) ===
  # A long malformed tunable crashes a SUID binary (proof it parses attacker input):
  env -i 'GLIBC_TUNABLES=glibc.malloc.mxfast=glibc.malloc.mxfast=AAAA..(very long)..' /usr/bin/su --help
  # A segfault in ld.so confirms the parser reaches the vulnerable path.

=== PUBLIC PoC ===
  git clone https://github.com/leesh3288/CVE-2023-4911
  cd CVE-2023-4911 && gcc -o exp exp.c && ./exp
  # Other PoCs: RootkitSmith/CVE-2023-4911, drmchen, flyyy chain the overflow to a root shell
  # by corrupting ld.so state so a chosen library/symbol runs as root.

=== TARGET BINARY ===
  # Any SUID-root dynamically-linked binary works as the vector; /usr/bin/su and
  # mount/umount/sudo are common. ls -la /usr/bin/su to confirm the SUID bit.

=== ALTERNATIVES ===
  dirtypipe / overlayfs CVE-2023-0386 / nf_tables CVE-2024-1086   # other local root chains

defense.why_it_works: glibc's ld.so sanitizes GLIBC_TUNABLES for SUID binaries but a bug in __tunables_init() mishandles an attacker-controlled tunable of the form name=name=value, overflowing a stack buffer during loader initialization. This happens before the SUID program drops privileges, so memory corruption executes with root's effective UID.
defense.prerequisites: A local unprivileged shell and any SUID-root dynamically-linked binary. Vulnerable glibc 2.34-2.38 (default on Fedora 37/38, Ubuntu 22.04/23.04, Debian 12) with no 2023-10 patch.
defense.impact: Reliable local privilege escalation to root on default installations - one of the most widely exploitable Linux LPEs of 2023 because the vector (SUID + stock glibc) is near-universal.
defense.detection: [MITRE T1068] Processes spawned with a GLIBC_TUNABLES value containing a repeated tunable name (name=name=) or an abnormally long value; SUID binaries (su, mount, sudo) crashing in ld.so; a root shell parented to an unprivileged process immediately after a short-lived SUID exec.
defense.artifacts: auditd execve records capturing GLIBC_TUNABLES in the environment; core dumps / dmesg segfault entries for ld.so inside SUID binaries; EDR process-tree showing uid=0 child of an unprivileged user.
defense.splunk_spl:
index=linux sourcetype="linux:auditd" type=EXECVE
| search a0="*GLIBC_TUNABLES*" OR proctitle="*GLIBC_TUNABLES*glibc.malloc*"
| table _time, host, auid, exe, proctitle
defense.sentinel_kql:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where ProcessCommandLine has "GLIBC_TUNABLES" and ProcessCommandLine has "glibc.malloc"
| project TimeGenerated, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, ProcessCommandLine
| sort by TimeGenerated desc
// repeated tunable name (name=name=) overflowing ld.so in a SUID binary
defense.sigma_rules: lnx_glibc_tunables_suid_overflow (GLIBC_TUNABLES repeated-name overflow against a SUID binary)
defense.prevention: Patch glibc to the fixed build (Fedora glibc-2.38-11+, Ubuntu 2.35-0ubuntu3.4 / 2.37-0ubuntu2.1, Debian 2.36-9+deb12u3) released 2023-10-03. Where patching lags, strip the SUID bit from non-essential binaries and deploy with the hardened loader. Monitor auditd execve for GLIBC_TUNABLES.

detections.name: GLIBC_TUNABLES overflow against SUID binary (Looney Tunables)
detections.logic:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where ProcessCommandLine has "GLIBC_TUNABLES" and ProcessCommandLine has "glibc.malloc"
| extend repeated = ProcessCommandLine has "=glibc.malloc.mxfast=glibc.malloc.mxfast="
| where repeated or strlen(ProcessCommandLine) > 400
| project TimeGenerated, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine
detections.false_positives: Legitimate tuning of glibc.malloc via GLIBC_TUNABLES is rare and never uses a repeated tunable name.
detections.tuning: Alert on the repeated name=name= pattern or abnormally long values; allowlist known performance-tuning wrappers.
